To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have mapped and sequenced the mutations responsible for the RNA- temperature-sensitive phenotype of three complementation group F ts mutants of Sindbis.
the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase activity is encoded by nsP4 and that the nsP2-nsP4 complex is involved in the initiation of RNA synthesis.
the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase of Sindbis virus is encoded by nsP4, that nsP4 and nsP2 interact, and that nsP4 has a Gly-Asp motif.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of RNA synthesis of alphavirus and flavivirus.
the identification of the viral proteins involved in viral RNA synthesis.
mapping and characterizing the temperature-sensitive (ts) mutations of Sindbis virus (SIN), which is a member of the alphavirus genus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ts6, ts118, and ts110 have a lesion in nsP4 and ts118 also has a lesion in ns2P.

nsP2, nsP3, and nsP4 are required for viral replication and that nsP2 is involved in the initiation of replication, nsP3 is involved in the elongation of the RNA chain, and nsP3 and nsP4 together are involved in the termination of replication.
the ts phenotype of the three known group F mutants was the result of mutations in nsP4 and that the ts phenotype in ts118 resulted from the interaction of two mutations, one in nsP2 and one in nsP4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ts mutants in complementation group F have mutations in nsP4 which are the cause of their ts phenotype.
the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase of Sindbis virus is nsP4.
nsP4 of Sindbis virus is the viral RNA polymerase, and that it is the only viral protein involved in RNA replication, which is a process that is temperature sensitive in ts6, ts 110, and ts 118.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have mapped the RNA temperature-sensitive mutations to the viral genome.
the nsP4 gene is essential for RNA synthesis and that the nsP2 gene may play a role in this process.
the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) of Sindbis virus is encoded by nsP4, and that the RdRp is the only viral component required for RNA synthesis.
